figures.caption: Figure 1: Accuracy and runtime scaling with the number of input frames. Although existing acceleration methods substantially reduce end-to-end runtime, they incur pronounced camera-pose degradation under the strict AUC@3 metric. GPA-VGGT achieves comparable runtime while maintaining camera-pose accuracy close to that of vanilla VGGT.

Figure 2: Two sources of accuracy degradation in existing token-merging methods. Top: Query merging collapses the block-12 outputs of 8383 tokens into 1212 shared outputs, whereas retaining all queries while merging only K/V preserves the output diversity of the unmerged model. Bottom: Omitting the +log⁡s+\log s correction disproportionately allocates attention to the first frame. Restoring the correction recovers an attention distribution close to that of the unmerged model.

Figure 3: Effect of cross-frame context in the early blocks. Top: Replacing global attention with frame attention substantially displaces the block-8 output field from the full-global-attention reference, whereas the shared cross-frame K/V set largely preserves it. Bottom: Pairwise alignment of per-frame drift directions. Cross-frame special tokens partially align the drift, and image-token summaries further reduce its variation, preserving a coherent geometric reference across views.

Figure 4: Overview of GPA-VGGT. Early blocks 00–88 replace global attention with frame attention augmented by a shared cross-frame K/V set containing special tokens and content-adaptive pooled image-token summaries. Later blocks 99–2323 preserve all queries and merge only K/V tokens, using a weaker merge ratio in the core blocks 1313–1616. (a) Pooled summaries are constructed by assigning patch tokens to stride-8 seeds according to cosine similarity and averaging the K/V tokens within each content-adaptive cluster; the summary size determines the +log⁡s+\log s correction. (b) K/V matching is computed after a 128128-dimensional Gaussian projection, while all queries are retained for global attention.

Figure S1: Core-block selection on VGGT. Each point shows how much the final global-block output changes from the unmerged model when the indicated contiguous block set is protected from merging; lower values mean smaller changes. The criterion is computed without ground-truth annotations across four datasets. Blocks 1313–1616 consistently give the smallest change and are selected as the core-block set.
